name: Vortx AI
description: Spatial AI lab; maker and maintainer of the emem protocol. Encode on device, decode with @emem: don't move your files, deliver tokenised context. Satellites, telescopes, rovers, drones, robots, cameras and machines keep their files; emem encodes each observation as one signed, content-addressed token (nine token shapes: emem:fact:, emem:cell:, emem:entity:, emem:bundle:, emem:raster:, emem:cube:, emem:rasterset:, emem:trace:, emem:attestation:; plus emem:state: and emem:tree: addresses); agents pass the token, never the file, and @emem decodes it straight into their context (ChatGPT, Claude, Salesforce Agentforce, Dify, any MCP client), so every agent cites the same bytes instead of a drifting paraphrase; any receiver resolves it, hashes the bytes, verifies the ed25519 receipt and can recompute the value from the raw source (https://vortx.ai/ decodes one live token in the hero; https://vortx.ai/#run runs six devices' published samples end to end in the browser; https://vortx.ai/#connect encodes a file on the visitor's device with nothing uploaded; https://vortx.ai/#decode catches a drifted number; https://vortx.ai/proof/ runs every check step by step and re-derives one live example of every token shape). emem is Apache-2.0, free to read, verifiable offline. geo.qa is the same memory on a private tenant. The planned satellite signs at the instrument, on a published plan with deliberately no date. The only thing for sale is team time: free office hours, a paid integration session, a sovereign session.

skills.name: Read verifiable Earth memory
skills.description: Resolve a place to a stable ~10 m cell address and read signed, content-addressed facts about it (vegetation, water, heat, forest change, and more). Reads need no key or account; every fact verifies offline via ed25519 signature and blake3 address. Use the emem MCP server or HTTP API.
examples: Recall the NDVI fact for Bengaluru and cite its emem:fact: token.
Was this parcel cleared before we sourced from it? Check the forest record.

skills.name: Encode a device's file as emem tokens
skills.description: Keep a large file (a satellite scene, a robot log, a drone or camera video) on the device that made it and publish only its pointer.v1 note: 4 MiB ranges, a blake3 hash per range, one Merkle root. The note's name is base32(blake3(note)[0:16]) and its rows are addressed as emem:tree:<cid26>#row=<i>, so an agent reads the note and fetches only the ranges it needs, each checked against its row. Encode with https://vortx.ai/tools/emem_point.py (or in the browser at https://vortx.ai/#connect, nothing uploaded); publish in your own namespace with `ememdev write`.
examples: My user has a 2 GB downlinked scene; give them the commands to encode it and publish the note instead of the file.
Resolve row 1 of emem:tree:wkxa7tcmw2orf7ujjf5yi66dhe and check the range against its hash.
